messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: TalentOps <talentops@redwood.ai>

Subject: Principal Serving Engineer — upcoming onsite & quick alignment request

Hi team,

We have Priya Shah (referred via TalentBridge) scheduled for an onsite loop next Tuesday (10/6). Amber from TalentAgency included the candidate resume in the thread; I attached a copy and a draft scorecard (redwood_principal_serving_scorecard_v2.docx). Before everyone interviews, can we do a 30‑minute alignment to harmonize expectations on scope and leveling so feedback is comparable?

Key asks:
- Confirm top 3 focus areas for interviewers (system design, low-latency inference internals, leadership/roadmap)
- Agree on what separates L5 -> L6 (concrete examples we can probe)
- Align on interview structure and timeboxes (40/20/20 or similar)

Proposed slot: Mon 10/5 10:00–10:30am PT (I’ve tentatively added a calendar hold — see attachment). If that doesn’t work, share availability.

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Principal Recruiter, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Principal Serving Engineer — upcoming onsite & quick alignment request

Thanks Marissa — this is important. I can do the Monday slot. High level from hiring manager POV:

1) Role scope: This hire will own cross-team inference performance — runtime optimizations, kernel selection decisions, and rollout/guardrail patterns for quantized models. Not an infra ops hire; they must demonstrate deep inference engineering (latency vs throughput tradeoffs) and influence product roadmaps.

2) Leveling: L6 = drives architecture and tradeoffs across multiple product lines, mentors other engineers, defines the signals we use for SLA tradeoffs. Concrete probes: ask for examples where the candidate chose a quantization strategy and why; ask them to design fallback routing for degraded GPUs.

3) Interview flow: I prefer 60m split: 30m whiteboard/design, 20m past experience/deep dives, 10m behavioral/leadership. Scorecard: emphasize impact metrics and cross-team influence.

I’ll bring two concrete prompts to the alignment meeting: a short system design (KV cache eviction + multi-model routing) and a past-project deep dive rubric.

- Laura
--
Laura Bennett
Director, Serving Engineering
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Principal Serving Engineer — upcoming onsite & quick alignment request

Agree with Laura. Quick additions as bar-raiser:
- Leveling clarity: L6 must show examples of tradeoffs where they accepted increased cost for latency or vice‑versa with measurable outcomes (numbers matter). If candidate cannot give concrete metrics or tradeoffs, lean toward L5.
- Red flags: inability to explain kernel/ops behavior, vague answers on production rollouts, or no evidence of mentoring/ownership.

Focus areas for interviews I’ll cover: system design probing around failure modes and rollout strategies; cross-team influence and post‑mortem ownership.

I’ll join the Monday meeting and bring a short calibration checklist for scoring consistency.

— Rishi
Bar-Raiser, Infrastructure
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Principal Serving Engineer — upcoming onsite & quick alignment request

(Conference call notes pasted below)

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 10:00 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick alignment notes from today (10/5 10:00am PT) — summary from Evelyn:
>
> - Agreed focus areas: 1) Inference runtime & kernel decisions (40%), 2) System design for low-latency/high-throughput (30%), 3) Leadership/mentorship + cross-team impact (30%).
> - Leveling guide: see bullets below for L5 vs L6 distinctions to use in the scorecard.
> - Interview format: 60m per loop; 30m design, 20m past work, 10m leadership/values. Timeboxes to be enforced; interviewers should capture "Candidate claim", "Evidence", "Gap" on the scorecard.
>
> L5 vs L6 (agreed):
> - L5: strong individual contributor; has built components with measurable improvement; influences peers inside a team.
> - L6: owns cross-team architecture choices; provides concrete metrics/experiments; mentors several engineers; negotiates tradeoffs with product/infra.
>
> Example probes:
> - "Describe a time you improved tail latency — what experiments did you run and what was the result?"
> - "How would you design fallback routing if a quantized model yields degradation on certain inputs?"
> - "Tell us about a time you changed a deployment pattern across teams; how did you convince stakeholders?"
>
> Action items:
> - Marissa: ensure candidate packet + final scorecard to interviewers (done).
> - Rishi: share calibration checklist (will attach).
> - Laura: finalize two design prompts and share tomorrow.
> - Markus/Evelyn: confirm interviewer timezones and pads for breaks.
>
> Attachments: PriyaShah_Resume.pdf; redwood_principal_serving_scorecard_v2.docx

> —Marissa

Notes from Evelyn (added): please be explicit about numbers during the interview (QPS, p95/p99 improvements) and request artifact evidence where possible (links to PRs or perf dashboards). If candidate cannot provide numbers but has plausible methodology, capture that as "could be coached" versus "no evidence".

— Evelyn
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Priya Shah — loop notes

Candidate: Priya Shah — onsite loop 10/6
Interviewers: Laura (design), Evelyn (runtime probes), Markus (past projects), Rishi (bar-raiser check)

Summary: Strong systems background, clear experience with inference runtime optimizations at scale. Good example where candidate reduced p99 tail latency by 35% through batching/kernel selection and root-cause analysis. Leadership evidence: led cross-team rollout for model sharding and adoption across two product teams.

Concerns: Candidate’s quantization experience is more research-prototype oriented; limited in shipping quantized kernels to prod. Felt confident they could partner to ship, but might need initial support.

Recommendation: Consensus leaning L6 with a development plan to ramp into quantized production work. Action: Rishi to run final calibration and update scorecard.

Attachments referenced: candidate slides (candidate shared link), interview notes in scorecard.

— Markus
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Principal Serving Engineer — interview feedback: Priya Shah (initial loop)

I reviewed the scorecard and raw notes and ran the calibration checklist. My call: clear L6 on system scope and cross-team impact. The quantization hands-on gap is coachable; we should add a short onboarding goal (first 90 days) to pair with existing kernel owners and own a small quantized path.

Decision: Recommend hire at L6. Marissa — please proceed with offer routing and include the 90‑day ramp objectives in the candidate packet.

— Rishi
Bar-Raiser, Infrastructure
